subject.title: Enhancement: Allow custom safe headers in fetch-guard cross-origin redirects

question: Should OpenClaw introduce an operator-controlled way to retain custom headers such as `x-api-key` across cross-origin fetch-guard redirects, and if yes must it be scoped by destination origin rather than a global safe-header extension?
rationale: The requested behavior intentionally changes a credential-forwarding boundary and adds public config surface, so automation cannot choose the trust model or acceptable guardrails.

options.title: Design scoped operator policy
options.body: Allow the capability only with header-name validation, destination-origin scoping, docs, and tests that keep default behavior strict.

options.title: Keep strict stripping only
options.body: Reject the new config surface and keep custom credential-like headers blocked on all cross-origin redirects.

options.title: Add global header extension list
options.body: Implement the requested shape directly, accepting the higher risk that any allowed header can be replayed to any redirect origin.

recommendation.title: Design scoped operator policy
recommendation.body: Allow the capability only with header-name validation, destination-origin scoping, docs, and tests that keep default behavior strict.

likelyOwner.reason: The current strict behavior traces to steipete's security hardening commit, and the remaining choice is about changing that trust boundary.
